title: Shared pretend with objects already alternated turns at 19 months in one kindergarten
summary: A kindergarten study found shared pretend with objects organized as turn-taking already in a group whose average age was 19 months.
body: Fantasia, Moncalli, and Bello filmed spontaneous play among children from 19 to 28 months in one kindergarten. Sequences where children coordinated actions on pretend objects were already built as alternating turns in the youngest group, whose mean age was 19 months. The play was mostly functional, such as using a toy pot or a doll's cloth for its everyday pretend job, not a long spoken story. Children often waited until a partner's action was nearly finished, and they watched each other more than they talked. The authors call the work exploratory. It is one setting with familiar Western play objects, not a census of pretend play.

sources.title: Shared construction of social pretend play sequences at the kindergarten
sources.author: Valentina Fantasia, Francesca Moncalli, and Arianna Bello
sources.note: Supports turn-alternation in co-constructed object pretend at 19 months, and the mostly functional character of the play. CC BY 4.0. Paraphrased.
